deepDiveThesesUsed.summary: Apps advertise '60+ supported models' but the vendored llama.cpp build only recognizes specific LLM_ARCH_* tags, so many trending releases (e.g. Qwen3.x) silently can't load.

The GGUF quant label (e.g. Q4_K_M) is not a standardized artifact — different quantizers (and even a vendor's own official QAT release) produce measurably different quality/size under the identical nominal tag.

The app's July 10 Swift rewrite fixed the July 7 staleness gap by fetching llama.cpp's latest GitHub release at build time instead of a pinned old commit, but that fetch resolves 'latest' fresh every build with no pinned tag and no version ever surfaced to the user, so two builds cut hours or days apart can silently embed different sets of supported architectures with no way to tell which one shipped. Backed by real llama.cpp release-cadence data (3 tags in under 3 hours) and PR merge-time data (~1 day to 24 days depending on whether an architecture is genuinely new). Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-07 thesis: static staleness vs. dynamic non-determinism.

PrismML's Bonsai 27B ternary/1-bit quantization of Qwen3.6-27B is real, Apache-licensed research with genuine download traction (74K/559K downloads), but its actual downloadable ternary file (7,165,121,600 bytes = 7.17GB, verified via HF tree API) is 21% heavier than PrismML's own advertised 5.9GB, and the Q2_0 group-128/64 packing scheme it uses has zero reader in any tagged llama.cpp release as of b10054 (2026-07-17) -- GitHub Discussion #22019 proposing mainline support has sat open/unanswered since 2026-04-16, with the author's own 'PRs this upcoming week' promise (2026-04-22) still unfulfilled 3 months later. Distinct from the three prior engine/quant theses (arch gating, quant-label variance among already-supported formats, version pinning): this is about a format with no mainline path at all, not a supported-but-inconsistent or stale-engine problem. Every load-bearing claim independently re-verified beyond the initial research-agent pass (direct HF API byte counts, full discussion-thread text, PR #8151 merge date).

CRITICAL GAP: the new native engine is NOT version-pinned. scripts/fetch-llama.sh always downloads whatever is the LATEST ggml-org/llama.cpp GitHub release at build time — no tag/commit is recorded anywhere in the repo, the resulting Frameworks/llama.xcframework is gitignored (not committed), there is no CI that would capture which version went into any given build, and no App Store release/tag exists yet for the native app. Until fetch-llama.sh is pinned to an explicit tag/commit (recorded in-repo) or a real App Store release ships with recorded engine version, catalog-compatibility checks in this routine work from whatever llama.cpp's actual current 'latest' release supports, since that's the only defensible reference for what a fresh build would fetch today.

DEEP-DIVE: Bonsai 27B (PrismML, ternary+1-bit quantization of Qwen3.6-27B, released 2026-07-14). Independently re-verified every claim beyond the initial research pass rather than trusting the subagent's summary: pulled exact byte counts via Hugging Face's tree API for both prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf (Q2_0 group-128: 7,165,121,600 bytes = 7.17GB vs PrismML's own advertised 5.9GB, a 21% gap; Q2_g64: 7,585,330,240 bytes, 5.9% larger than Q2_0, matching maintainer ggerganov's April prediction of 'less than 6% extra memory' almost exactly) and prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf (Q1_0 1-bit: 3,803,452,480 bytes = 3.80GB, close to the advertised 3.9GB -- this tier's size claim holds up, unlike the ternary tier's). Read the full text of GitHub Discussion #22019 ('Supporting Ternary Bonsai in llama.cpp', opened 2026-04-16 by PrismML's khosravipasha, ggerganov's group-64 counterproposal 2026-04-21, khosravipasha's agreement + 'PRs this upcoming week' promise 2026-04-22) -- confirmed still open/unanswered on GitHub as of today, three months later, no PR ever filed despite PrismML shipping the group-64 file itself. Confirmed PR #8151 (merged 2024-09-06, unrelated pre-existing CPU-only BitNet-style TQ1_0/TQ2_0 ternary types) for context on what llama.cpp already supports vs. what Bonsai actually needs. Deliberately dropped an uncertain claim from the initial research pass about PR #11183's current CUDA-kernel merge status after getting conflicting signals across sources -- cut per 'can't source it, cut it' rather than risk an inaccurate claim on a side detail not load-bearing to the thesis. Benchmark retention numbers (95%/90% claimed) presented as explicitly self-reported/PrismML-only, with the structural point that third-party reproduction is presently hard to obtain since no released engine can load the files being scored. Distinct thesis from all three prior engine/quant posts (07-07 arch gating, 07-09 quant-label variance among already-supported formats, 07-13 version pinning) -- this is about a format with zero mainline reader at all. Both pieces self-graded against the hook-score rubric (concrete numbers in the first two sentences, no genre throat-clearing, contrarian/surprising angle) since no /post-grader skill is available in this session's skill listing -- consistent with every prior run.

A second candidate (oomwoo, an open-source build-yourself robot vacuum) was ruled out outright: its own builder confirmed the robot's runtime autonomy is classical SLAM/Nav2 navigation, not an on-device language or vision model, so it doesn't fit the series at all regardless of its genuine local-first/Home-Assistant merits. Neither cleared the bar; recording both here so a future run either does the verification work HookProbe still needs (a real embeddable photo, independent traffic-classification claims) or looks elsewhere rather than re-discovering the same candidates from scratch. No DIY spotlight published this run -- a normal, expected outcome per quality-over-cadence, not a gap in the search (two research agents covering Hackster, GitHub, Raspberry Pi's own blog, exo/NetworkChuck, Habr, HN and r/LocalLLaMA between them).
